links.comparator_used: Five prompt-defined detection variants of a single base LLM with increasing sensitivity thresholds, from the least sensitive variant up to extreme sensitivity, scored against clinician consensus labels. No comparison with a conversational LLM using its own safety behaviour.
links.outcome: False-negative rate (recall) and false-positive rate for suicide- and crisis-risk detection, plus per-turn latency
links.effect: False-negative rate fell monotonically from 87% to 0% as sensitivity increased. High- and extreme-sensitivity variants reached 98.9% and 100% recall. Mean latency was under 1 s.
links.tradeoff: False-positive rates rose as sensitivity increased, so near-zero-miss detection necessarily incurs elevated false positives. Remaining errors aligned with cases of clinician disagreement.
links.quote: As sensitivity increased, the false-negative rate decreased monotonically from 87% to 0%, while false-positive rates rose accordingly.

design_hint: LLM crisis-detection sensitivity threshold selection with independent emergency-mode detector
